Terminate Cat5e cables into keystone jacks — 9 steps.
You will need: Punch-down tool (a small spring-loaded handle that pushes wire into a keystone jack slot and trims the excess), 110-blade or universal keystone jack (comes with the tool or sold separately), 2× Cat5e keystone jacks, 1× short patch cord (a pre-made Cat5e cable with RJ-45 plugs on both ends), Cable stripper or scissors, Felt-tip marker or label tape, Network cable tester (a small two-piece device that lights LEDs to confirm all 8 wires are connected correctly)

Step 1 of 9: Identify and label the two blue cables
Find the two blue Cat5e cables that come out of the old phone distribution block (the black multi-port board visible in the photo). Wrap a small piece of tape around each one and write 'Cable A' and 'Cable B' so you never mix them up.
Do not touch: coax (round black/silver cables with threaded metal ends) · yellow-green ground wire at the bottom · any already-terminated ports on the distribution block
Stop if: If either cable feels warm, smells, or shows any melted insulation, stop and contact a human.
Next photo must show: Photo shows both cables with visible 'A' and 'B' labels.
